The *Vipattivāra* (Pvr 2.11) is an analytical section of the *Parivāra*, the final book of the Theravāda *Vinaya Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. Structurally, it analyzes the disciplinary rules by relating them systematically to the different categories of "falling away" (*vipatti*) or failure in monastic conduct [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records three modern translations across two languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

No curated parallels in other Buddhist traditions are recorded by SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches with score ≥ 10 [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies extensive text reuse comprising 109 matching passages across 13 texts, all situated within the Vinaya's *Parivāra* [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial overlaps occur with the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4, sharing 46 passages), other *Vipattivāra* sections (notably Pvr 1.11, Pvr 2.3, and Pvr 1.3), and recurring Parivāra analytical treatises such as the *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 2.16, Pvr 2.8, Pvr 1.8), *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), *Adhikaraṇavāra* (Pvr 2.14), *Saṅgahavāra* (Pvr 2.12), *Samuṭṭhānavāra* (Pvr 2.13), *Samathavāra* (Pvr 2.15), and *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 2.10) [DharmaNexus].

The passages retrieved from secondary literature do not examine this specific text, matching only the broad lexical term *vipatti* in separate contexts such as general Vinaya classifications, Abhidhamma karmic conditions, or meditation defects.
